podcast.title: Audition for Velvet Revolver (2003)
podcast.body: Travis Meeks of Days of the New was considered and tried out by the members of the band that would become Velvet Revolver for the lead singer position before Scott Weiland was brought in, but he was not selected. "The guys had already tried out...Travis Meeks of days that the new and neither them worked out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation as a Supergroup (2003)
xref.body: Formed in 2003, Velvet Revolver began with former Guns N' Roses members Duff McKagan, Slash, and Matt Sorum, who then recruited Dave Kushner from Wasted Youth. They auditioned several singers, including Josh Todd of Buckcherry, Travis Meeks of Days of the New, and B-Real of Cypress Hill, before settling on Scott Weiland. "Susan told Mary that three guys from Guns and Roses had kissed and made up and were forming a new band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Travis Meeks Auditions for Velvet Revolver (2003)
xref.body: The frontman of Days of the New, Travis Meeks, was one of the singers considered and tried out by the future members of Velvet Revolver for their lead vocalist role before Scott Weiland joined. "The guys had already tried out...Travis Meeks of days that the new and neither them worked out."
